sdf_to_occupancy — 3D transform op

• Data kinds: sdf → voxel

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sdf_to_occupancy(sdf, iso=0.0) (to call the implementation directly, import match3d; match3d.sdf_to_occupancy(sdf, iso=0.0); from the registry, ops3d.get("sdf_to_occupancy"))

Usage

SDF → an occupancy voxel volume (at or below iso = inside = 1). The way back from an SDF to voxels.

An op that is nothing but (sdf <= iso).astype(float64). Under the signed_distance_field convention (inside <0), iso=0.0 gives inside=1, outside=0. The equality is included, so a voxel exactly at iso counts as inside. A positive iso gives occupancy dilated outward by iso voxels, a negative one gives shrunk occupancy (equivalent to isotropic dilation/erosion if the SDF is a true distance). It also works on the output of tsdf_from_depth (in front of the surface +, behind −, unobserved +1) with the same iso=0.0, but unobserved regions end up on the 0 side (outside). Any input shape is accepted; returns float64 of the same shape (0.0 / 1.0). NaN compares false and therefore becomes 0 (no warning).

★If you pass a label volume, the background becomes "inside". backends_typed.TYPE_TO_SORT folds sdf / labels / voxel into the same volume, so wiring the output of label_components or vol_label straight in raises no exception. Labels use 0 for background and 1 or more for foreground, so <= 0 is the background itself. Measured (2026-09-08, 24³ cube, true inside 1,728 voxels): passing the SDF gives 1,728, passing 0/1/2 labels of the same shape gives 9,504 (5.5x) —— the sign is inverted. To build occupancy from labels, write labels > 0 yourself instead of using iso.
